title: Picking up tunes in the Lewis band and keys
summary: He learned tunes by ear with relative pitch while sitting in; George called keys; Jim sometimes played in the wrong key.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: He was able to teach you a tune by telling you the name of the chord or by showing you? Or both. Uh, let's see now.

Well, I picked up a lot of the tunes just by sitting down and, and Lewis, Lewis would, would kick off tunes, you see. And I didn't even know the tune. Uh, and, uh, I just play, you know. Uh, and, uh, I had this air, you see. And I could, uh, catch chordal relationships and key relationships. Uh, it's relative pitch. It's having relative pitch. And I could catch these things very easily. And so I had no trouble in picking up these things because usually ninety percent of the, of the traditional things were very simple harmonically, if not melodically, you know. It's, uh, same, uh, in the same way the traditional classics are. The Baroque classics are very simple harmonically. They're very simple to hear. You know. But what the voices are doing is something else, you know. But, and the same thing in New Orleans jazz. And it was very easy to hear the harmonic progression.
I don't remember ever really going through any prescribed method of learning a tune. Would George call the key?

Yeah, yeah. George would usually say B flat concert, you know. We wouldn't say concert, say B flat meaning concert, naturally. And the band would just kick it off. Sometimes it'd just say this tune. And since the band had been, it just called the name of a tune, and since the band had been playing it for so long, they'd just kick it off in the right key. Sometimes, I remember Lawrence told me something, and I realized later on, sometimes Jim would go through two choruses of playing in the wrong key. And finally he realized that he'd been in the wrong key. You see. This is always pretty funny. But those are the kind of things that Lawrence didn't like, and those are the kind of things that Lawrence told me that Bunk couldn't stand when he funded the band. I think...
